title: Wanted to highlight our take on Critical Hits our Pokémon Ranger inspired Roguelite, called Spell Unbound.
author: AlkrssveGames
selftext:
I wanted to touch on some of our combat systems/mechanics. Today we'll discuss Critical Hits, or rather binds, which is probably one of my favorite implementations of a core gameplay system in the game. Since almost all of the combat is restricted to drawing loops, there is no head or weak spot to aim at, and there is no parry or counter-attack window to allow for us to let this type of system shine.

So, how did we approach this? Simple, through what we call precision. Each loop that you close has a couple of stats attached to it; *precision* is how close, percentage-wise, your loop is to a perfect circle. The closer you are to 100%, a perfect circle, the higher your Crit Chance. Now, there is a floor to entry and a ceiling to this system. Entry starts at 75% precision, giving the player 10% Crit Chance, and reaches a ceiling at 90% precision, capping Crit Chance at 30%.

You might be wondering why stop at 90%? Why not go all the way to 100%? The short answer is we did, just not in the same way as our 75%-90% window. Although unlikely and especially not consistently so, we realized that precision above 90% could be achievable. So to reward the sheer patience, accuracy, and overall luck it would take to reach near 100% precision, we made a second Crit window. Instead of scaling, we gave it a flat Crit Chance, so for any players that manage to get at least 95% precision, they get a guaranteed Crit.
